newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwanda genocide tribunal offers high pay for staff.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda genocide tribunal offers high pay for staff.

text.p: The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda (ICTR) advertised for staff on Wednesday, offering large salaries and perks even for positions such as stenographers.
Newspaper advertisements sought courtroom stenographers for minimum annual salaries of $41,272 plus entitlements for hardship and mobility, rent, education, home leave and family visits.

The average salary for a stenographer in the region with an international company is about $1,000 a month without perks. In government, a stenographer would receive about $300 a month in government with benefits such as housing, transport and leave.
The tribunal also sought security officers with minimum annual salaries of $35,784 in addition to the entitlements.
Officials at ICTR headquarters in Arusha, northern Tanzania, declined to respond to questions about the high salaries but U.N. agencies in the region pay more than the private sector.

The ICTR was set up by the United Nations in 1994 to bring to trial suspects accused of leading the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutus in the tiny central African nation of Rwanda.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan dismissed two top tribunal officials in January after a U.N. report detailed administrative mismanagement, unqualified staff and legal chaos at the ICTR.
